text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi has told a Farmer's Association conference that a situation where farmers who produce bumper crops are at the mercy of low prices offered by private traders, will not be tolerated.
-- The Mekong Delta provinces of Long An, Kien Giang, An Giang and Dong Thap will likely lose 216,000 of their total 678,000 hectares of paddy because of flooding.
-- Greece plans to open an embassy in Vietnam in 1998.
-- Vietnamese and Laotian finance ministers have signed a memorandum of understanding on financial co-operation.
-- The government will prepare a draft law on awards for individual achievement during the economic reform process to submit to the National Assembly.

-- National Assembly Vice Chairman Dang Quan Thuy has told a visiting U.S. delegation that Vietnam considers the search for missing American servicemen a humane issue, and expects the United States to help Vietnam overcome the consequences of war.
-- Another trial related to Vietnam's biggest-yet drugs-trafficking case will open on August 20 in Hanoi.
